content: The test image shows soybean seeds — one normal tan seed and one with dark brownish-black mottled/moldy discoloration covering the upper portion of the seed. This is seed-level pathology. Top candidates: Purple_Seed_Stain, Phomopsis, Diaporthe.

The test image shows two soybean seeds — one normal and one with severe dark brownish-black mottled discoloration with rough texture across the seed surface. 

Key observations:
- **Affected part**: Seed (not leaf/stem/pod)
- **Color**: Dark brown-black mottled pattern, rough/textured surface
- **Pattern**: Concentrated on the upper/dome portion of the seed

Comparing references:
- **Purple_Seed_Stain**: Shows seeds ranging from light purple blotching to very dark/near-black seeds — matches well, including the very dark seed visible in the top-right panel of that collage
- **Phomopsis**: Shows pod-level circular lesions, not isolated seed discoloration
- **Diaporthe**: Shows stem cankers — not seed pathology

The dark mottled discoloration on the seed is consistent with Cercospora kikuchii (Purple Seed Stain), which can manifest as dark purple to nearly black rough discoloration on seed surfaces.
